title: Chandialias, Jandialias and Those who harmed the Gurus' cause and the Sikh Panth And those Given to Debauchery…

blocks.text: (Dear Readers) listen to the episode of extremely wicked persons, Who deserve to be included among the earliest crop of villains. Those who tried to eclipse the Gurus and harm the Sikh Panth, And who had been slandering and vilifying the devout Sikhs. (1)
lines: (Dear Readers) listen to the episode of extremely wicked persons,
Who deserve to be included among the earliest crop of villains.
Those who tried to eclipse the Gurus and harm the Sikh Panth,
And who had been slandering and vilifying the devout Sikhs.

blocks.text: Of those whom the (great) Guru gave his blessings gratis, And those who failed to assimilate and imbibe Guru's message. Of those who wished to destroy the very same source, From which they had sprung up (and got sustenance). (2)
lines: Of those whom the (great) Guru gave his blessings gratis,
And those who failed to assimilate and imbibe Guru's message.
Of those who wished to destroy the very same source,
From which they had sprung up (and got sustenance).

blocks.text: Let me, first of all, narrate how he originated, Thereafter, I would reveal his (evil) thoughts and deeds. A "Ghanag"3 Jat (by caste), a Sultani (by faith), a resident of Jandiala was he, Who lived a life of extreme deprivation and raggedness. (3)
lines: Let me, first of all, narrate how he originated,
Thereafter,
I would reveal his (evil) thoughts and deeds.
A "Ghanag"3 Jat (by caste), a Sultani (by faith), a resident of Jandiala was he,
Who lived a life of extreme deprivation and raggedness.

blocks.text: He came to know that the Guru ran a free community kitchen, Where people flocked and ate food to their hearts' content. Irrespective of the fact whether one rendered any service or not, There was no dearth of any provisions and eatables there. (4)
lines: He came to know that the Guru ran a free community kitchen,
Where people flocked and ate food to their hearts' content.
Irrespective of the fact whether one rendered any service or not,
There was no dearth of any provisions and eatables there.

blocks.text: Hearing this, proceeded he to the Guru's abode there, And joined the (dedicated) band of Guru's cooks and kitchen crew. There, he kneaded flour and kept the kitchen fires burning. And had had his fill as many times as he wished to eat. (5)
lines: Hearing this, proceeded he to the Guru's abode there,
And joined the (dedicated) band of Guru's cooks and kitchen crew.
There, he kneaded flour and kept the kitchen fires burning.
And had had his fill as many times as he wished to eat.

blocks.text: But he could not exorcise the ghosts of his Sultani past from his mind, Nor could he thoroughly imbibe the Sikh spirit in his character. Mind is cleansed of dross only after the Sikh spirit is embedded in it, As rigorously as rust deposited on a sword is rubbed with a chisel file. (6)
lines: But he could not exorcise the ghosts of his Sultani past from his mind,
Nor could he thoroughly imbibe the Sikh spirit in his character.
Mind is cleansed of dross only after the Sikh spirit is embedded in it,
As rigorously as rust deposited on a sword is rubbed with a chisel file.

blocks.text: But having departed from his homestead at an auspicious moment, He became worthy of (great) Guru's blessings gratuitously. Having been blessed with all the boons with Guru's (single) glance, This rustic Hindal Jat could not contain the Guru's benediction. (7)
lines: But having departed from his homestead at an auspicious moment,
He became worthy of (great) Guru's blessings gratuitously.
Having been blessed with all the boons with Guru's (single) glance,
This rustic Hindal Jat could not contain the Guru's benediction.

blocks.text: One day His Holiness (Guru Amadas) leaving his Divine seat), Paid a visit to the quarters running the community kitchen. As the devout Sikhs paid obeisance at the Guru's lotus feet, This Hindal Jat also rushed to bow at the Guru's feet. (8)
lines: One day His Holiness (Guru Amadas) leaving his Divine seat),
Paid a visit to the quarters running the community kitchen.
As the devout Sikhs paid obeisance at the Guru's lotus feet,
This Hindal Jat also rushed to bow at the Guru's feet.

blocks.text: As the other (fellow) Sikhs ventured to touch the Guru's feet, The Hindal Jat found his hands covered with wheat flour. Lest Guru's sacred feet should get smeared with wheat flour, He decided to pay his obeisance in his own way. (9)
lines: As the other (fellow) Sikhs ventured to touch the Guru's feet,
The Hindal Jat found his hands covered with wheat flour.
Lest Guru's sacred feet should get smeared with wheat flour,
He decided to pay his obeisance in his own way.

blocks.text: Folding his (flour-covered hands) behind his back, He placed his head on the Guru's feet in a kneeling posture. The Guru, impressed by his (rare) gesture of thoughtfulness, Caste a benevolent glance on him considering his devotion. (10)
lines: Folding his (flour-covered hands) behind his back,
He placed his head on the Guru's feet in a kneeling posture.
The Guru, impressed by his (rare) gesture of thoughtfulness,
Caste a benevolent glance on him considering his devotion.

blocks.text: Responding benevolently to such a thoughtful gesture, The Divine Guru showered his blessings on this Hindal Jat. (Thus), such a small (sensible) gesture brought so many rewards, That he became worthy of Guru's grace gratuitously. (11)
lines: Responding benevolently to such a thoughtful gesture,
The Divine Guru showered his blessings on this Hindal Jat.
(Thus), such a small (sensible) gesture brought so many rewards,
That he became worthy of Guru's grace gratuitously.

blocks.text: Such gratuitous rewards may, fall to anyone's lot, But noble human vessels alone can preserve such rewards. A pitcher made of unbaked clay can never hold water, Whatever strategies one may adopt for its preservation. (12)
lines: Such gratuitous rewards may, fall to anyone's lot,
But noble human vessels alone can preserve such rewards.
A pitcher made of unbaked clay can never hold water,
Whatever strategies one may adopt for its preservation.
